patient_response: I start projects and assignments full of ideas, but I just can’t seem to follow through and finish things, and it’s already cost me my first job. I'm here because I really need to understand why I can't seem to complete tasks reliably despite wanting to.

They became a major crisis over the last year when my responsibilities at the startup ramped up, but looking back, I've struggled with this since childhood. Even in elementary school, my report cards always said I was "bright but daydreams, forgets homework, and talks out of turn," and I was constantly losing worksheets and blurting out answers.

I wouldn't say I've felt persistently sad or lost interest in my hobbies, but losing my job was a major blow to my confidence and left me incredibly frustrated. I have pulled back from social activities, but that's really more out of shame and embarrassment over my recent struggles than a lack of interest.

No, I wouldn't say I experience that kind of constant, everyday worry. Any stress I have is pretty much entirely focused on my inability to get things done and losing my job, rather than worrying about my health or other general things.

Well, to be honest, I’ve started eating big amounts by myself at night because I’m embarrassed for anyone to see how much I’m eating. It’s just so hard for me to admit, but I really needed to talk to someone about it.

No, I don't do any of those things like throwing up, fasting, or over-exercising after I eat. I've never tried to get rid of the food or make up for it that way. I usually just sit there in my recliner feeling awful about what I've done.

Yes, I definitely do. Once I start eating, it feels like a switch flips and I'm just on autopilot, telling myself "Belinda, stop," but my hands keep fixing another plate anyway. It really doesn't feel like I'm the one deciding when I'm finished.

It’s been happening at least once or twice a week for about five months now. It really started around the time my daughter and youngest grandbaby moved out of state and the house got so quiet in the evenings.

My mind just won’t shut off about work and everything else, and I can’t seem to turn the worrying off no matter what I do. A friend suggested I should talk to a professional, so I decided to finally come in.

It's been going on for about nine months now, starting right around the time I got promoted at work. I took on a lot of heavy new responsibilities, like being the primary bilingual contact for a major corporate client and mentoring new hires, and it quickly felt like I could never truly disconnect.

I wouldn't say I feel deeply sad or down, but I have been skipping things I normally love, like my weekly dance nights and hiking. I've been canceling plans with friends mostly because I feel completely drained, exhausted, and just too anxious to keep up with anything outside of work.

Yes, definitely. I feel constantly wired and on edge, like I've had way too much coffee, and I'm always clenching my shoulders or tapping my foot. My sleep is also terrible; I lie awake until 2 a.m. replaying work scenarios and wake up feeling like I never actually rested.

It definitely goes beyond just work. My brain constantly runs worst-case scenarios about all sorts of things, like my parents' health, my student loans, or saying something stupid while mentoring. It feels like there's always some disaster I'm about to cause or miss.

I'm not currently taking any medications, and I don't have any medical conditions like thyroid issues. I also don't actually drink much caffeine at all, even though I constantly feel wired and on edge as if I've had way too much of it.

I'm here because of a warehouse collapse that happened on a job site about five months ago. Since that collapse on the job, I can’t bring myself to go into certain buildings or walk under unfinished structures without feeling like I have to get out immediately.

Yes, out of nowhere I’ll suddenly hear my coworker screaming and see the mezzanine coming down in my mind like it’s happening all over again, making my heart pound so hard I have to step outside just to catch my breath. When I do finally fall asleep, I constantly jolt awake at the slightest creak in the house, terrified that something is collapsing again.

Yes, my mood has completely changed, and I carry this constant heavy sense of dread and guilt with me. I've become so tense and withdrawn that I have a very short fuse with my husband, snapping at him over simple things. It has caused a lot of arguments, and we barely spend any time together anymore.

Yes, I'm constantly on edge and walk around with this heavy dread, feeling like something terrible is about to happen. I'm incredibly jumpy, to the point where the slightest creak in my house makes me jolt awake thinking the roof is collapsing. This constant high alert keeps me so tense that I'm on a very short fuse with everyone, especially my husband.

Ever since I got shocked on that job, I feel this constant sense of dread and uneasiness that just won’t go away, even when I’m not at work. It's just... always there in the background, and I can't seem to shake it.

Yes, I do. Out of nowhere during the day, I’ll suddenly see myself back on that concrete floor staring at my dead arm while the guys are yelling for help, and my chest tightens up like it's happening all over again. I also wake up sweating in the middle of the night from these half-remembered nightmares about work, and I can't get back to sleep after that.

Yes, absolutely. I make up excuses to stay in the office doing paperwork or send the younger apprentices to open panels instead of me. Just the thought of standing in front of live gear makes my stomach flip, and I just can't bring myself to do it.
The actual shock happened about six months ago. I tried to shrug it off and joke about it at first, but these symptoms have really been building up and constant for about the last four months.

Yes, absolutely. I feel completely wired and jumpy, like I'm constantly on guard and waiting for something terrible to happen. Even when I'm in safe places, like sitting on the couch with my wife or trying to watch a ball game, I just can't shake that feeling.

For almost two years I’ve been certain certain people in the music scene are secretly coordinating to destroy my career, and nothing anyone says changes that. I just need someone to actually look at what is happening to me.

No, I have never heard or seen things that weren't there. My senses are completely fine, and my mind is clear. This is about the actual things these people are doing to sabotage me, not some kind of hallucination.
No, I have never felt like my thoughts were being broadcasted or that any outside force was controlling me. My mind and body are entirely my own, and I am fully in control of them.

No, my motivation and interest in my daily work are actually completely fine, and I'm still writing music on deadline and running rehearsals smoothly. I don't have any general loss of interest or emotional issues. It's just that I get completely derailed and consumed whenever an email or meeting involves the people I'm suspicious of.

Everyone keeps saying I’m overreacting, but I know certain people in town are targeting me, and nothing anyone shows me changes what I know is true. My family basically forced me to come here because they think I'm crazy, but I know what is actually going on.

This all really started a little over a year ago, right after I lost my sales job and had to move back in with my relatives. It has been happening consistently ever since then, and it hasn't let up at all.

No, I’ve never heard voices or seen things that aren't actually there. My mind is completely clear, it's just that these people in town are actually coordinating against me and I can see the real-world proof of it.

No, my thoughts are perfectly organized and I haven't lost any motivation at all. If people would just stop acting like I'm crazy, they'd see I can handle normal day-to-day things like helping around the house, running errands, and taking care of myself without any issues.

No, absolutely not, my thoughts are completely my own and no one is putting ideas in my head or broadcasting them. I’m just observing the real things that people around town are actually doing. It's all based on real actions I see with my own eyes.
I keep seeing that explosion in my head like it’s happening all over again, and I can’t shut it off. It just plays over and over, and I'm really struggling to get through the day with it.

The explosion happened about 14 months ago, so a little over a year now. I've been having these flashbacks pretty much ever since the accident, and instead of fading over time, they've just dug in and become a part of my everyday life.

Yeah, I do. I'll drive the long way around just to avoid older buildings or that side of town where it happened. And if anyone at church brings up the accident or asks about apprentices, I just shut down the conversation or walk off because I can't stand feeling all that come up.

Yes, I'm completely wired and barely sleep, usually lying awake until two or three in the morning before waking up shaking from the same fire nightmare. If someone drops a tool on the job or slams a car door, I jump out of my skin and my heart starts pounding like crazy. It takes me a really long time to stop shaking because my body just feels on edge all the time.

Yes, I feel completely numb inside. I used to live for playing basketball with the guys and helping with the church youth program, but now I just go home and stare at the TV because nothing feels fun anymore. Even when my little niece runs up to hug me, I feel totally detached, so I've just pulled away from everyone because I'm too exhausted and on edge.

I keep starting audit tasks and then somehow not finishing them or missing key steps, even when I’m trying my absolute best to follow through. It's gotten to the point where it's seriously impacting my job, and I'm just feeling incredibly overwhelmed by it all.

While these issues became really disruptive about two years ago after my promotion, they actually trace all the way back to my childhood. Looking back, my elementary school teachers often commented on me daydreaming, rushing through math problems with careless mistakes, and constantly chatting or fidgeting instead of staying in my seat.

I don't really experience constant, uncontrollable worry about a variety of different things in my daily life. However, I do get quite anxious specifically about making mistakes or missing critical details at work.

No, I haven't been feeling persistently down, sad, or hopeless. I also haven't lost interest in my hobbies like my dance classes—it's just that I've had to cut back on them because I'm spending all my extra hours trying to keep up with work.

It's a bit embarrassing to admit for someone who works in construction, but as soon as I know I have to go up high on a building, I get an overwhelming rush of fear. The moment I even approach the scaffolding, I just can't seem to handle it.

No, I've never actually had a fall or any specific accident. It really just started about eleven months ago when I got moved to a new crew doing high-rise renovations, which was a major jump from the single-story jobs I'd always done before.

No, it's strictly limited to being up high, especially on the scaffolding, lifts, and upper floors at work. I don't have any issues at all with crowds, public transit, or enclosed spaces. It is really just the heights that trigger this fear.

I do everything I can to stay on the ground, like trading shifts and losing overtime, but if I'm forced to go up, I just freeze on the ladder and feel completely sick. It's really hurting my career because I had to skip a mandatory training tower test, and now I'm being passed over for the promotions and higher-paying roles I've been working toward.

No matter how interested I am, I can’t keep my attention on job training or applications long enough to finish them, even though I really want to work on cars. I recently forgot an important intake appointment for an automotive program I'd waited months for, which made my sister—who has ADHD—urge me to get evaluated. I'm just so frustrated because I feel like I'm completely stuck.

Yes, absolutely, it goes all the way back to elementary school. My teachers were constantly moving my seat and sending notes home because I'd blurt out answers, wander the classroom, and always lose my homework or forget instructions. I wasn't trying to misbehave or cause trouble, but I just couldn't seem to stay on track even back then.

Yes, definitely—my legs are always bouncing, my feet are tapping, and I'm constantly messing with pens or keys without even realizing it. If I'm forced to sit still for too long, I get this pent-up energy where I feel like I have to get up and pace just to take the edge off. My family actually jokes that I can never just "chill" because I'm always on the move, starting multiple things at once.

Yes, it's caused a lot of tension since I had to move back in with my parents, because they constantly nag me and think I just don't care when I forget bills or chores. I also tend to interrupt and cut them off during family discussions about my plans or money, which visibly annoys them and leaves me feeling really ashamed.

They have definitely been consistent throughout my life rather than coming and going in phases. It goes all the way back to elementary school when I was always losing homework and wandering around, but it has become way more overwhelming and disruptive over the last two years as I've tried to manage adult job and financial responsibilities.

I keep getting these sudden, vivid memories of the train crash that pop into my head and completely derail whatever I’m doing. It happened a little over two years ago, and I've realized I just can't "power through" them on my own anymore.

Yes, I’ve basically built my whole life around avoiding anything to do with trains. I’ll drive an extra hour in traffic instead of taking the Metro-North, and I refuse to book client meetings if they are near a station. I even have to change the TV channel if a subway scene comes on because my chest starts tightening just from the sound of it.

Yes, all of those have become major issues for me. I lie awake wired until 2 or 3 AM tensing for an impact, and when I do sleep, I'm constantly jerked awake by awful train nightmares. I'm also always on edge, flinching at loud noises and scanning every room, and my fuse is so short now that I keep snapping at my boyfriend and coworkers over the smallest things.

My outlook on everything has definitely taken a really dark turn, and I constantly feel like the world is just a rigged game where disaster can strike out of nowhere. I've lost all confidence in my own competence and feel like I can't even trust my own commute. I'm also plagued by this endless self-blame, constantly thinking that if I hadn't stayed late at work that night or had somehow pulled the emergency brake, I could have prevented the whole thing.
I’ve started going out of my way to avoid any job that involves getting up high. When I absolutely can’t avoid it, I’m barely able to stay up there long enough to do my work.

It’s strictly heights that get to me, like ladders, roofs, or high tree stands. I don’t have any trouble with crowds, public transit, or being far from home at all. Even my volunteering and fishing are only affected if they involve getting up high.

The doctors keep telling me nothing is there, but I know they put something inside me and they’re hiding it. I know for a fact that it's in my shoulder, and I'm just so tired of being lied to by everyone at that clinic.

This has been going on for about nine months now, starting right after I went in for a routine shoulder scan. I am absolutely certain they slipped that device in during that procedure, and it's been nearly a year of me trying to prove it while they keep covering it up.
No, nothing like that at all. I don't hear any strange voices or see things that aren't there. My head is completely clear, it's just this physical device in my shoulder that they are hiding from me.

I still manage to go to my work shifts, handle the bills with my wife, and chat normally with my coworkers. However, over the last nine months, I've turned down extra work hours and stopped going on fishing trips or family get-togethers. I feel like I have to spend all my free time in my workshop building detection rigs to prove this implant is in me.

No, my thoughts are completely my own and my mind is perfectly clear. Nothing is controlling how I think or making my thoughts jumbled. It's just this physical device in my shoulder that's the problem, and I'm the only one trying to find it.

Hi doctor. I’m here because I can’t sit through long production meetings or edit sessions anymore—I keep getting up and pacing even when I know I should stay in my seat. It's starting to really impact my career as a camera operator and editor, especially since I'm trying to move into a senior role.

This isn't a new issue; it actually dates back to my childhood. Even in elementary school, teachers constantly told my parents that I couldn't stay in my seat and was always getting up to sharpen my pencil or wander around while other kids worked. It's always been there, but it has only recently become a major problem for my career with these long meetings.

It’s definitely a physical urge rather than worry or anxiety. I get this crawling, pent-up energy in my body, almost like I'm in the wrong gear, and I physically feel so wound up that I just have to get up and move. Even on my days off when I’m just trying to relax on the couch, I can’t sit still for more than ten minutes before I have to get up and do something.

Yes, I definitely do. On tight deadlines, I often make careless mistakes like missing obvious color notes or typos in lower thirds because I skimmed too fast, which forces me to re-export cuts. Also, during production meetings, I'll completely drift off thinking about shot ideas and have to ask people to repeat themselves, even though I was looking right at them.

Yes, and it's honestly pretty embarrassing. On set or in meetings, I have a bad habit of cutting people off and blurting out suggestions before they've even finished explaining the problem. I also find myself jumping into other people's conversations at festivals or leaning over a colleague's shoulder to comment on their edit uninvited, and afterward I always worry I came off as really rude or pushy.

I can't recall the exact age or if it was precisely before I turned seven, but it was definitely happening early on in elementary school. I vividly remember teachers complaining to my parents that I was constantly getting up to sharpen my pencil or wandering the classroom while everyone else was sitting quietly.

Since I started this job and the tech program at the same time, I feel like I’m not handling the pressure well and it’s messing up my school and work. It's just been really hard to balance everything lately, and I need some help figuring out how to manage it.

I’d say I feel more constantly on edge and worried about keeping up rather than deeply depressed. The pressure just feels like too much, so I end up avoiding my classes and zoning out on my phone while beating myself up about it.

Yes, they definitely started right after all those major changes. Before that, I was actually excited and busy with my normal life, but this has only been going on for about a month since the job, the move, and the program all hit at once.

The anxiety itself is definitely driven by trying to keep up with the job, school, and my move, rather than random worries. However, it has spilled over in the sense that I’ve completely stopped doing my hobbies, like basketball and painting, because I just feel too overwhelmed. So the pressure from work and school is making me withdraw from the rest of my life.

This is definitely the first time I’ve ever felt like this. Normally, I handle things pretty well and don't get this overwhelmed. All of these changes happening at once is just unlike anything I've dealt with before.
I haven't really noticed those specific physical symptoms like a racing heart or muscle tension. It's more that I just feel completely mentally overwhelmed, on edge, and shut down by everything.

No, I haven't had any thoughts like that at all. While I do feel extremely overwhelmed, stressed, and disappointed in myself right now, I definitely don't want to hurt myself or feel like life isn't worth living.

No, I haven't had any crying spells or felt hopeless or deeply sad. Instead, I just feel constantly on edge, extremely overwhelmed, and frozen or shut down. When it gets to be too much, I just avoid my tasks and zone out on my phone rather than feeling depressed.

I know it doesn’t make sense, but the thought of going into any kind of medical office or having tests done scares me so much that I keep putting off appointments I really need. It's gotten to the point where my primary doctor suggested I talk to someone, so that's why I'm here today.

It is definitely the environment and the procedures themselves that terrify me, rather than a fear of being sick. Just the physical act of walking into a clinic or the thought of lying in one of those machines makes my stomach drop. Even when I know it's just a routine check-up, the dread of being in that medical setting is what completely panics me.

Yes, it has definitely been longer than six months. This intense fear started about thirteen months ago, right after I slipped on some ice, fractured my wrist, and had to go to the emergency room. Ever since that visit, the dread of anything medical has been a constant struggle for me.

No, I don't have any flashbacks or nightmares about the fall or the ER visit itself. It's not that I'm reliving that day, but rather that I feel this intense dread and anxiety about any future medical appointments or going into clinics.

My primary care doctor urged me to come here after a routine department physical flagged some issues, but I'm really struggling with this. To be honest, I’m scared that if I start eating more, I’ll lose control and put on weight I can’t afford at my age and in my line of work.

I severely limit what I eat and never have episodes of overeating or trying to get rid of it. Most days I just get by on a black coffee in the morning and maybe a small piece of chicken or an apple late at night. Sitting down to a full meal just feels like I'm breaking discipline, so I avoid it.

Yes, my recent department physical flagged my weight as being significantly low, and my pants are hanging off me so much that I've had to punch extra holes in my duty belt. Even so, I still feel this constant urge to tighten up even further to avoid getting sloppy on the job.

When I look in the mirror, I don't see a skinny guy; I just see a gut and flabby arms that make me feel like a failure as a cop and as a man. Keeping that number on the scale from going up feels like the only thing I still have any real control over in my life.
I’m convinced a former client has quietly used my ideas to structure things so I’m being pushed out of my own field. I know how it sounds to others, but I simply can’t be talked out of that belief.

No, this concern is strictly focused on that specific former client and the people in their immediate professional network. I don't have any issues trusting my family, friends, or others in my life. Outside of this situation, my daily routines, my painting, and my social interactions are completely normal and unaffected.

No, I have never experienced anything like that. I've never heard voices, seen things that weren't there, or had any other unusual sensory experiences. My mind and perceptions are completely clear in that regard.
This has been going on for about eleven months now. It started shortly after I finished a major advisory contract with that client and began transitioning into semi-retirement.
No, I haven't experienced anything like that. My mood has remained quite stable, and I haven't had any prolonged depression or unusual highs over these past eleven months.

I don't use any recreational substances, and I only drink alcohol in moderation, perhaps a glass of wine now and then. I'm not on any major prescription medications, and my physical health has been excellent with no recent issues.

I keep losing track of what I’m supposed to be working on and can’t seem to stay organized with all the tickets and follow-ups at my job. Ever since we shifted to a high-volume, rapid-response model, I've been really overwhelmed, and a recent configuration mistake actually landed me on a performance improvement plan. My supervisor suggested I get evaluated, which is why I'm here today.

Looking back, I’ve actually struggled with this kind of distractibility and restlessness since I was a kid, though my job's new high-volume pace has made it much worse lately. Back in elementary school, my teachers always wrote notes home about me daydreaming, blurting out answers, and not finishing worksheets. My parents even used to joke that I could never sit still long enough to do my homework without wandering off.

Yes, they definitely spill over into my personal life. My wife gets very frustrated with me because I constantly forget to pay bills, call the plumber, or confirm appointments until a late fee or reminder shows up. Even trying to relax with a book or movie is hard because I feel too restless to just sit still, and it gets really uncomfortable.

No, I wouldn't say I have constant, uncontrollable worry about a lot of different things. I definitely get stressed and frustrated about the specific things I mess up or forget at work and home, but it's not a general, everyday anxiety.

I keep getting caught up in nagging, unwanted thoughts about past decisions and what terrible things might happen, and it’s making it hard to enjoy my retirement. I used to really appreciate the quiet of my post-work years, but lately, these worries have just been taking over.

Yes, I do. To calm myself down, I find myself repeatedly going over old email folders, loan forms, and genealogy notes, rereading them line by line or silently reciting reassurance phrases about having been careful. I can't seem to stop until it feels "just right," even though I know it's unreasonable for things that are long since settled.

I haven't timed it exactly, but I often lose entire evenings to these thoughts and checking routines once the house gets quiet. It takes up so much time that my poetry writing has slowed to a trickle, and I've even started skipping neighborhood gatherings because of it.

No, I haven't really felt persistently sad or empty. My main struggle is just the constant anxiety and preoccupation with these unwanted thoughts and checking routines. It feels more like a restless worry than a deep sadness.
I go to great lengths to avoid getting on an airplane, even when it means missing important family events. It has really started to limit my life, so I finally decided to come in and get some help.

It is really a mix of both. The idea of being sealed in a metal tube at 30,000 feet with no way out terrifies me, making me feel like I'd be signing my own death warrant if I got on a plane again. I vividly picture the plane dropping out of the sky, which instantly makes my heart pound and my hands go clammy.
No, not at all. I have absolutely no trouble with buses, trains, elevators, or crowded places. This intense fear is strictly limited to flying and being on an airplane.

I'm here because I can’t shake the belief that my spouse and friends have been secretly plotting behind my back, no matter how much they deny it. My couples therapist suggested I come get an individual evaluation to talk about it, so here I am.

No, I've never had issues trusting people in the past, so this definitely isn't a lifelong thing. These specific suspicions about my spouse and friends only started about a year and nine months ago. It all began during a really stressful store remodel at work when I was traveling a lot and we were arguing about our time together.
No, I definitely don't hear voices or see things that aren't there. My concern is strictly about the secret plotting and the behaviors of my spouse and friends.

No, my thinking is completely clear and my motivation is totally fine. I still run my store smoothly, manage my staff, and handle all of my daily responsibilities without any issues. The only real problem I'm facing is the suspicion and tension this is causing with my spouse and friends.

Ever since they changed my position at the shop, I just can’t seem to adjust, and it’s throwing off my work and my whole routine. It feels like everything has been turned upside down, and I'm really struggling to get a grip on it.

The change at the shop happened about a month ago when they restructured my position. I started feeling this way almost immediately—within a week or two of being switched to the new line and supervisor. It has been going on constantly ever since then.

Yes, I've been feeling incredibly defeated and on the verge of tears, and I've completely lost interest in the things I used to love. I've stopped paddle-boarding and playing pickleball, and instead of working on my metal sculptures, I just sit on the couch staring at my unfinished work.
I haven't really noticed any major changes in my sleep patterns. I just feel incredibly drained and defeated after a shift at work, like I have absolutely no energy left for anything else.

I haven't really noticed any significant changes in my appetite or weight. And while I feel incredibly unmotivated and defeated right now, I haven't had any distinct issues with my concentration itself.

I don't really feel worthless or blame myself for the restructuring, since those changes were completely forced on me by the company. I mostly just feel incredibly defeated, overwhelmed, and frustrated by these new quotas and how they've thrown off my entire routine.
No, I haven't had any thoughts of hurting myself or wanting to die. I'm just feeling incredibly overwhelmed and stuck with this whole work situation right now.

No matter how much I rest, I feel completely drained and can’t keep up or focus at work anymore. It has gotten to the point where I'm falling behind on my shifts at the clinic, and I just can't seem to shake this exhaustion.

Yes, most days I wake up with this heavy, sinking feeling like there's a dark cloud on my chest, and I feel sad and hopeless for no clear reason. I've also completely lost interest in things I used to love, like jogging and my Raspberry Pi projects. Now, I just end up sitting on the couch scrolling on my phone all evening because I can't find the energy to care.

The constant exhaustion and low mood have been really bad for about a year and a bit, though things started building nearly two years ago. It began when my clinic upgraded to a new electronic health record system right as I started evening classes for my LPN. Staffing shortages hit soon after, and picking up extra shifts to help out just pushed me past my limit.

Yes, I constantly feel like a terrible person and a bad nurse's aide who is putting patients at risk. My sleep is a mess because I lie awake with my mind spinning and then wake up around 3 or 4 AM unable to drift off again. On top of that, my appetite has plummeted; I mostly just push my food around and throw it away, to the point where my coworkers have noticed my scrubs are hanging off me.
No, I've never experienced anything like this before this current period started about two years ago. This is really the first time in my life I've ever felt this way.

I feel like I’m always on guard and tense, like something bad is about to happen every time I’m out in the neighborhood. An older pastor at my church recently noticed my visible tension and how I've been avoiding certain ministry tasks, and I realized I just can't keep functioning in my calling while feeling constantly on edge like this.

Yes, about two years and three months ago, I was caught in a drive-by shooting on my block where a teenage boy I knew was shot just feet away from me, and I had to drop to the ground fearing for my life. That night is exactly what keeps me constantly on guard now. Anytime I hear a car backfire or a siren, it pulls me right back to that sidewalk, and it feels like it's happening all over again.

It’s definitely because I’m terrified of being reminded of the shooting and having all those awful memories come rushing back. I plan my entire day to avoid that specific corner and being out after dark so I don't have to face those feelings or constantly scan for danger. It's not really about having a panic attack, but more about trying to keep myself from reliving that night.

I spend so much time checking and rechecking how I look at the gym and before going out that it’s taking over my days. It has gotten to the point where it's completely taking over my schedule and I just can't seem to stop.

It's not really about my weight or body shape, but I'm obsessed with how crooked my face looks and how weird my jawline is from the side. I end up spending hours zooming in on photos and checking every mirror to try and hide those specific parts before anyone can see me.
No, it's strictly about how I look. I don't have any rituals like handwashing or checking locks; all of my checking is just about fixing my hair, changing clothes, and trying to hide my face.

I’ve had some self-consciousness about my looks for a long time, but it got really severe recently. It escalated when my soccer teammates started posting high-resolution photos and workout videos of us on social media. Seeing myself frozen in those action shots made me start obsessing over how my face and jawline look from different angles.

I'm not entirely sure of the exact number of months, but it has definitely been building up over a while now. It really started getting out of hand once those photos and videos started going up online.

Yes, my friends and sister tell me they don't see anything wrong with my face or jawline at all, but their reassurance doesn't help at all. I still feel incredibly anxious and continue to spend hours zooming in on photos and obsessing over how crooked I look. No matter what they say, I just can't stop seeing it.

It’s had a huge impact on my life because I’ve been missing work shifts and turning down hours because I get stuck checking myself. I’ve also been canceling soccer matches and salsa nights because I'm terrified of people seeing me from the wrong angle. Now, my sister and my friends are constantly bringing up how I’m never around anymore.

No, I don't worry about it being a medical illness or disease at all. My concern is strictly about how it looks visually because I'm just deeply self-conscious about how crooked my face looks and how weird my jawline appears from certain angles. It just makes me feel like I look completely wrong.

Yes, it has definitely been going on for much longer than six months. It started as a long-standing self-consciousness about my appearance that I've had for years, and it has just gradually worsened over time to get this bad.

I can’t stop thinking about how bad I look, especially my face and stomach, and it’s gotten to where I don’t want people to see me anymore. It's just really hard to even leave the house lately because I feel so embarrassed.
